label: Philip J. Corso
narrative:
Corso is the case where the primary record is both stronger and weaker than the claim made for him, and a node is the only place a reader sees both halves. His own DA Form 66, released by US Army Reserve Personnel Command in April 1998, puts the Army's Foreign Technology Division in his service record: staff officer in the division from 20 July 1961, then 'Chief Foreign Technology Div, OCRD USA' from 18 April to 18 July 1962 -- three months. The same form places him at Fort Riley, Kansas from 21 April 1947, which covers the alleged 6 July 1947 observation, and records him as an Intelligence Staff Officer on the Operations Coordinating Board in Washington from 24 February 1954 to 1957.

His 322-page FBI release is the other half. Searched in full, the words UFO, flying saucer, unidentified, Roswell, extraterrestrial and saucer appear zero times. What the file does contain is independent corroboration of the OCB posting from a source that is not Corso: in 1955 Gen. Arthur S. Trudeau told the FBI that 'Colonel Philip Corso, then assigned to the Operations Coordinating Board, would be in a position to elaborate' on a list of alleged Fabian Socialists, 'as he, Corso, had actually accumulated the information'. It also contains a 1964 episode in which Corso was found to be the source of a rumour that Oswald had been a paid FBI informant, and in which he 'emphasized the fact that his allegations had been strictly deductions and had no basis in fact'.

One line in his sworn statement does not survive his own service record. The affidavit says he 'was a member of President Eisenhower's National Security Council'. The DA Form 66 records the Operations Coordinating Board, which reported to the NSC and was not the NSC. That is a documentable overstatement in a sworn document, and this board carries it because the same record that supplies his strongest corroboration supplies it.
